subject.title: sessions_spawn from a CLI-harness parent (claude-cli) clamps subagents to gateway bridge tools — children lose exec/read/write

question: For CLI-harness parents, should subagent inheritance use the harness parent's native capability profile, skip bridge-runtime allow inheritance, or require an explicit opt-out/strict policy knob?
rationale: The source bug is clear, but choosing the wrong default can either keep breaking delegated coding or weaken subagent non-escalation for genuinely restricted parent sessions.

options.title: Model native harness capability
options.body: Treat CLI-harness native file/shell capability as the inherited privilege basis while preserving restrictive parent policies when they are explicit user or config constraints.

options.title: Skip bridge allow inheritance
options.body: Do not persist runtime bridge allowlists from CLI-harness parents, accepting that child runtime config becomes the main constraint for those spawns.

options.title: Add explicit policy control
options.body: Introduce a carefully documented subagent inheritance setting or strict mode, with upgrade-safe defaults and tests for both compatibility and non-escalation.

recommendation.title: Model native harness capability
recommendation.body: Treat CLI-harness native file/shell capability as the inherited privilege basis while preserving restrictive parent policies when they are explicit user or config constraints.
